In a two-derivative scalar sector with scalar values $\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n)$ in an open set $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, let $K\in C^\infty(\mathcal M,\mathbb R)$. Equality of mixed partials gives $d\omega_K=0$. With the standard complex structure on $\mathcal M$, a Kähler metric is a positive-definite Hermitian tensor whose associated real $(1,1)$-form is closed; hence on any open region where $g_{i\bar j}v^i\bar v^{\bar j}>0$ for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb C^n$, $g$ is a Kähler metric and $K$ is its Kähler potential. With $[\phi_i]=1$, the scalar kinetic potential has mass dimension $[K]=2$ and its Hessian has $[g_{i\bar j}]=0$, with coefficient dimensions assigned accordingly. Both kinds of data belong to the real D-term, not the holomorphic F-term.

Here $[\Phi_i]=1$, $[W_\alpha]=3/2$, $[g]=0$, $[\tau]=0$, the F-term integrand has mass dimension three, and the D-term integrand has mass dimension two; dimensionful coefficients in nonrenormalizable interactions carry the dimensions needed to make the density have mass dimension four. A Wilsonian prescription with cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$ formally separates Euclidean momentum modes with $|q|\geq\lambda$ from modes with $|p|<\lambda$. Consider a connected graph contributing to this chiral density, with $E_V$ external left-handed gaugino lines and $I_V$ internal vector lines. Uniformly scale the complete gauge-kinetic coefficient vector by a formal parameter $t$, $\boldsymbol\tau\mapsto t\boldsymbol\tau$, holding its coefficient ratios fixed. Each internal vector propagator then contributes $t^{-1}$. Let $A_m$ count pure-gauge vertices from the quadratic gauge-kinetic polynomial with $m\geq3$ vector lines; let $B_{mr}$ count vertices from a remaining F-term containing $r$ field strengths and $m\geq r$ vector lines; and let $C_m$ count vertices from the fixed canonical matter kinetic term with two chiral lines and $m\geq1$ vector lines. Every coefficient inside the square brackets is a positive integer. A graph contributing to the $\boldsymbol\tau$-independent part $H_\lambda$ must have $N_t=0$, so the bracket equals two. For the $B_{mr}$ case, [step 4.1]'s R-charge equation gives $E_V=r=m$; the vector-end equation then gives $I_V=0$. It is an original single tree insertion in $F_{\mathrm{rem}}$. A contribution to a holomorphic F-term cannot have an external antichiral line; with no other vertex type present, the two $C_1$ vertices therefore contract their two antichiral ends with their two chiral ends, giving $I_\Phi=2$, while the one $C_2$ vertex contracts its own chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Thus in each case the total internal-line count equals the vertex count and $L=1$; no matter line is external, so these graphs correct only the matter-independent quadratic gauge-kinetic polynomial, including any allowed Abelian mixing term. In the mixed case the end equation is $2I_V+2=3+1=4$, so $I_V=1$; the single $C_1$ vertex contracts its chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Hence $I=2$, $N_{\rm vert}=2$, and $L=1$. Its sole vector line is a bridge separating the gauge vertex from the matter vertex, so it is one-particle-reducible and excluded by the vertex convention in [F1]. Therefore every non-tree contribution to $H_\lambda$ is a one-loop shift of the matter-independent quadratic gauge-kinetic coefficient vector; no nonkinetic term in $H_\lambda$ receives a radiative correction. A contribution linear in $\boldsymbol\tau$ would require $N_t=1$, hence a zero bracket and no interaction vertices; it is absent. This proves equality for every positive-field-degree coefficient of $F_{\mathrm{rem},\lambda}$ and $F_{\mathrm{rem}}$; their constant coefficients agree by [A5].
